rationale: Reacher eval10 standard CEM reached 30%, while robust worst reached 10% and elite mean_std reached 0%.
TwoRoom eval10 standard CEM reached 60%, while robust worst reached 30%.
PushT eval3 standard and robust worst were both 0%.
The only apparent Reacher eval3 robust improvement was not stable when expanded to eval10.
Mean-only TTA did not explain the small eval3 worst/mean_std success, but compute-matched and larger-sample controls did not support a robust-scoring advantage.
A milder K=4/std=0.04/beta=0.25 Reacher run also reached only 10%.
interpretation.recommended_next_step: Do not promote robust CEM as an effective method from this pilot. If continuing, test full-budget Stage A only after adding a cheaper offline candidate-ranking analysis or identifying a setting where robust scores actually change top-k decisions without reducing clean performance.

purpose: Low-concurrency pilot for paper1/docs/ROBUST_CEM_CODEX.md robust CEM validation.
